dedupe_keys.name: pch guide to internet exchange point policy documents

description: This Packet Clearing House reference explains the policy documents with which internet exchange points (IXPs) define participation, operations and governance, and gives PCH's recommendations for each point. It notes that nearly every exchange has such a document, usually one or two pages in plain language, and distinguishes it from peering agreements, which are made between participants and concern the network layer, whereas the exchange policy covers the relationship between the exchange and its participants, mostly at the data-link layer. It prefers the word participants to members, because many exchanges are commercial, academic or governmental, not membership associations. The guide then walks through the clauses that are commonly found, or commonly discussed and rejected, such as eligibility, fees, mandatory multilateral peering, allowed traffic and equipment, and neutrality, and links to example wording from different exchanges where it diverges. Coverage: worldwide practice, drawing on PCH's support to exchanges in many countries. Format and access: web page in PCH's old wiki, free. Caveats: kept in an archive section of the PCH site and not dated, so some recommendations and example links may be out of date. Simulation uses: rules of access and peering for agent-based models of exchange growth and for scenarios of governance and membership. Related records: the PCH IXP directory lists the exchanges, and the ISOC study of exchanges in Kenya and Nigeria shows their impact.
